chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated this hadith in Kitāb al-Mashīkhah with another wording, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd.

He said: I performed ghusl on Friday in al-Madinah, put on my clothes, and applied perfume. Then a servant-girl passed by me, and I pressed my thigh against her, so I emitted madhy and she also emitted madhy. I felt distress because of that, so I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about it, and he said: There is no wudu (ablution) upon you, and there is no ghusl upon her.

The proper way to understand this report is that it is possible the listener erred in his hearing, and that he had only said, 'she emitted madhy,' but it occurred to him as 'she reached climax,' so he narrated it according to what he thought. It is also possible that he عليه السلام only answered him according to what appeared to him from his condition at that moment, and knew that he believed regarding his servant-girl that she had reached climax, while that was not so; thus he عليه السلام answered him according to what the ruling required, not according to his belief.

key_terms.اغْتَسَلْتُ: I performed ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal ruling applicable to the case
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which the event took place

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she emits fluid without actually reaching climax?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling related to sexual discharge and whether wudu (ablution) or ghusl becomes obligatory. It also includes a scholarly clarification reconciling the report by distinguishing between emission of madhy and actual climax, showing careful attention to legal precision in hadith transmission and interpretation.
